The Simplex rotor blades are straight in the radial direction, so even though tip leakage would produce some 3D effects, calculations could be performed two-dimensionally (2D) at the midspan.
Losses of 12% for partial admission and 5% for tip leakage were assumed for the 3D shrouded rotor analysis.
The initial bearing coolant circuit consisted of 4.5 lbm/sec of liquid oxygen (LOX) being diverted from the impeller discharge, with 1.8 lbm/sec leaking into the turbine disk cavity.
The redesigned bearing coolant circuit had 3.5 lbm/sec returning externally to the inducer inlet and 1.5 lbm/sec vented overboard.
The inducer design was modified to reduce the chord length by one-third, improving efficiency to 73% while also reducing the rotating mass outboard of the pump-end bearing.
The impeller design was found to be insensitive to small variations in the incoming flow angle, with the head coefficient varying from +10% to -7.5% about the design point.
The diffuser design was improved by cutting back the leading edge of the vanes to increase the flow angles and eliminate flow blockage, yielding a pressure rise of 288 psi.
The Simplex impeller generates a total pressure rise of 1,300 psi, with the radial impeller generating 85% of the required 1,500 psi discharge pressure.
The minimum inlet LOX pressure was 45 psi at 164°R flowing at 89.8 lbm/sec, yielding a required suction specific speed (Nss) of approximately 25,000 at the design point speed.
The turbine is designed to supply 700 hp at a wheel speed of 25,000 rpm.
The total mass flow rate through the turbine nozzles is 1.54 lbm/sec per nozzle.
The turbine inlet total temperature is 800°R, and the total-to-static pressure ratio is 15.
